- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to underpredict upward moves; increase forecast slightly above recent high.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model often overcorrects downward; adjust forecast upward to avoid deep sell-off bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 1–2% in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.3–0.7) and price is volatile, model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply a 1–3% downward bias to forecast mean.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true price by 1–3% in early-to-mid period; apply a 0.5–1.5% upward bias to first 10–15 days.
- When sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.5 → -0.5 → +0.5), model tends to lag; add 1–2 days of lagged sentiment to adjust forecast direction.
